overview: White adds 2.c4 to the Bird, building a Dutch-reversed or English-style structure with f4 and c4 and a later Nc3 and g3. Black usually plays 2...e6 or 2...g6, or hits e5 with 2...e5 3.fxe5 Ng4. The game is manoeuvring and flexible, with White trying to control e5.

white_ideas.idea: Control e5 with f4 and Nf3 and fianchetto the king bishop
Expand with c4, Nc3 and d3

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...e6 and ...d5 or fianchetto with ...g6
Strike with ...e5 to open the centre

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Dutch / English-style structure with c4 and f4

character.notes: Both sides develop normally with no forcing sacrifices.

soundness.notes: Sound if slightly weakening to the kingside.

structure.notes: Flank opening where the centre is not fixed.

approach.notes: A Bird line used occasionally; the Bird is a respectable surprise.

level.notes: Some knowledge of Dutch-style structures helps.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black strikes with ...e5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. f4 Nf6 2. c4 e5 3. fxe5 Ng4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gives a pawn for quick development.

character.reason: A flexible flank set-up with no early forcing play.

gambit.reason: No pawn is sacrificed in the main line.

soundness.reason: A sound if slightly loosening set-up.

structure.reason: Flank opening with an undecided centre.

level.reason: Requires understanding of reversed Dutch structures.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and fights for e5.
